text: In an effort to determine whether cell swelling mediates hypertrophic adaptations, Gundermann and colleagues (98) carried out a randomized crossover study whereby 6 young males performed a low-intensity resistance exercise bout with BFR consisting of 4 sets of leg extensions at 20% of 1RM and a similar low-intensity resistance exercise bout without BFR; at least 3 weeks separated the trials. During the non-BFR session, a pharmacological vasodilator (sodium nitroprusside) was infused into the femoral artery immediately post-exercise to simulate the cell-swelling response induced by BFR exercise.
